{"self_assessment": "Impact
I proposed the fish concept at the start and drew the sketch on the pad that the whole table built from. Choosing a big, simple outline with soft curves and a forked tail gave us a shape a judge should recognise at a glance. Stroke 1, which carries the start domino at the nose and runs along the top of the body, was mine, and it is the stroke every other piece depends on. As far as I can tell from my checks, all 118 standing dominoes connect to the start.

Execution
I laid the top body run myself and closed the joint after the first bend when Sofia flagged it. I then inspected the body and the notch between the tails several times, and found the whole fish connected from the nose. I noticed one slightly tight domino near the fork, judged it harmless, and left it alone rather than risk disturbing a working joint. We finished well before time and kept our hands off the build until the push.

Collaboration
I split the fish into four strokes so each person had a clear piece to build in parallel, and I sequenced the work so the tail pieces waited for the top run to connect. I kept the group informed about joints and the notch, and made sure people stayed clear of each other's areas, which helped limit bumps.

Leadership
I set the plan in the first minute, assigned strokes by name, and kept everyone coordinated through the build. When there were questions about the tail tip, I gave a clear direction: round it off and stop close to the other line without joining. I then called the hands-off point once the check showed everything was connected. The table finished calmly and on time.", "my_share_percent": 40}
